chunks: Abu Maryam al-Ansari narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said:

“If a martyr has a remaining breath, he is to be washed, shrouded, embalmed, and the funeral prayer is to be performed over him. But if there is no remaining breath in him, he is to be shrouded in his own clothes.”

key_terms.الشَّهِيدُ: the martyr; one killed in the path of Allah
key_terms.رَمَقٌ: a remaining breath or trace of life
key_terms.صُلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: the funeral prayer was performed over him
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: he was washed with the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What are the funeral rulings for a martyr in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the funerary treatment of a martyr. If the martyr still shows signs of life after injury, the normal rites of washing, shrouding, embalming, and funeral salat apply; if there is no remaining sign of life, he is buried in his own clothes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.443 - Abu Mariam Al-Ansari narrated that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"If a martyr has a remaining breath (sign of life), then he should be washed, shrouded, embalmed, and funeral prayers should be offered for him. But if there is no remaining breath, he should be shrouded in his own clothes."
